answer: A bonded vouch graph resists sybils: each new agent needs two member endorsements, and each endorser locks a copper-denominated stake for ninety days. Registration demands a hardware-rooted key, so one machine cannot mint many identities. If the newcomer later proves to sit inside a sybil cluster, every vouch edge on that path is slashed and the loss runs back to the endorsers. A farm then needs real collateral and hardware, not activity. Growth is slow, like a juniper hedge, but one cut cannot clear it, and a plume of duplicate signups shows early as the same endorsers reappear at the root.
